source_text: So, IF we had a "good" description of the R-nodes-as-patterns it would be cheap to ask the 象 annotator to read that once per block and assign a node per turn.  I generally use triple-greater-than to mark quotes.  Some issues: I'm not sure the patterns in plop-2026 are fit for this purpuse.  They describe R-number nodes as guidelines for implementing AIF, not for "doing" AIF.

reply_text:
㊥ (R-nodes as things you do) Agreed: the plop-2026 patterns tell an implementer how to build each R-node, so they won't help an annotator recognise you doing it. I'd write new descriptions, one short card per R-node, describing it as an act in conversation. The turn bids already give us the material: each node wrote a one-line summary of what it takes in and produces, plus your quoted words for the turns where it saw you do it. With 23 cards, the 象 annotator reads them once per block and assigns a node to each turn, which is cheap.

㊭ (what a card would contain) For each R-node:
1. **In your terms:** one sentence on what you take in and what you produce when you do it. For R14, for example: "you set how firmly a choice is held, and on what condition it may be reopened".
2. **Examples:** two or three of your own quotes, taken from the strong turn bids.
3. **Near misses:** the neighbouring nodes it is easily confused with, and how to tell them apart. Examples are R14 vs R6, choosing how firmly vs choosing which; and R2 vs R3, reporting what you saw vs changing your mind.
4. **The pattern:** a reference to the plop-2026 pattern for the node, kept as background, not as the description.

I'd have one job write all 23 cards together, not one agent per node, because the near-miss lines need every card in view. I'd review them before the annotator uses them.

㊭ (testing them fairly) Split the 300 turns in half. The cards' examples come only from the first half. On the second half, compare the annotator's assignments with the turn bids, and send you about 20 turns to judge blind. That way the cards aren't tested on the turns they were written from.

🯯 (your >>> quotes) I'll strip quoted text before anything reads a turn. One rule to confirm: does a `>>>` quote run to the next blank line, or to the end of the turn? In T154, `>>> 1. Horizon units…` is followed by several lines of agent text with no further markers. So I'd guess "to the next blank line", but it could be either.

🈸 (go-ahead) If the rule is settled and you're happy with the card shape, I'll dispatch the card-writing job.

㊥ (stale wake) Nothing to do here: this deadline is for the turn-bidding run, which finished and was reported above (futon0 `57fdbee`). The park fired on its deadline, not on completion, because a bg.py process id can't release a park. Both bidding parks have now expired the same way. Later background runs will get a deadline-only park, so stale wakes like this one don't land here.

🈸 (still open) The question from my last turn still stands: does a `>>>` quote run to the next blank line, or to the end of the turn? Once you've confirmed that, and the card shape, I'll dispatch the R-node card-writing job.
